name: Operating Systems & Systems Security
description: Kernel and OS-level security, isolation, sandboxing, virtualization, and access control.
narrative:
The earliest papers in this list, all from 2018, capture three concerns that would define the area. The most consequential is "Meltdown: Reading Kernel Memory from User Space" (USENIX 2018), which shattered the assumption that hardware memory isolation protects kernel space from user processes, kicking off a wave of microarchitectural-security research. Alongside it, the same year saw a strong push on finding kernel bugs before attackers do, with "MoonShine: Optimizing OS Fuzzer Seed Selection with Trace Distillation" (USENIX 2018) refining system-call fuzzing, and "FUZE: Towards Facilitating Exploit Generation for Kernel Use-After-Free Vulnerabilities" (USENIX 2018) automating exploitability assessment. A parallel thread tackled isolation and attack-surface reduction: "Debloating Software through Piece-Wise Compilation and Loading" (USENIX 2018) and "Effective Program Debloating via Reinforcement Learning" (CCS 2018) cut away unused code, while "Enforcing Unique Code Target Property for Control-Flow Integrity" (CCS 2018) tightened CFI defenses.

The second major theme, which quickly grew to dominate this set by citation count, is provenance- and audit-log-based attack detection. Even in 2018, "Towards a Timely Causality Analysis for Enterprise Security" (NDSS 2018) and "SAQL: A Stream-based Query System for Real-Time Abnormal System Behavior Detection" (USENIX 2018) framed intrusion investigation as a problem over system-event graphs, while "Dependence-Preserving Data Compaction for Scalable Forensic Analysis" (USENIX 2018) and "NodeMerge: Template Based Efficient Data Reduction" (CCS 2018) attacked the resulting data-volume problem. In 2019 this matured into real-time APT detection with "HOLMES: Real-Time APT Detection through Correlation of Suspicious Information Flows" (S&P 2019), and confronted the operational pain of false positives in "NoDoze: Combatting Threat Alert Fatigue with Automated Provenance Triage" (NDSS 2019), with "POIROT" (CCS 2019) reframing detection as threat hunting by aligning attack behavior to kernel audit records.

Across 2019-2020 the isolation and fuzzing threads kept advancing in parallel. "ERIM: Secure, Efficient In-process Isolation with Protection Keys (MPK)" (USENIX 2019) showed lightweight intra-process isolation using new hardware primitives, while "SANCTUARY" (NDSS 2019) and the cautionary "SoK: Understanding the Prevailing Security Vulnerabilities in TrustZone-assisted TEE Systems" (S&P 2020) charted both the promise and the fragility of ARM TrustZone enclaves. Kernel bug-finding sharpened around the hard case of concurrency, with "Razzer: Finding Kernel Race Bugs through Fuzzing" (S&P 2019), "HFL: Hybrid Fuzzing on the Linux Kernel" (NDSS 2020), and "Krace: Data Race Fuzzing for Kernel File Systems" (S&P 2020). On detection, "Unicorn: Runtime Provenance-Based Detector for Advanced Persistent Threats" (NDSS 2020) and "Tactical Provenance Analysis for Endpoint Detection and Response Systems" (S&P 2020) pushed graph-based methods toward practical EDR deployment.

The most recent papers show the field consolidating around learning over provenance graphs. "SHADEWATCHER: Recommendation-guided Cyber Threat Analysis" (S&P 2022) borrowed recommendation-system techniques, "PROGRAPHER: An Anomaly Detection System based on Provenance Graph Embedding" (USENIX 2023) leaned on graph embeddings, and "Kairos: Practical Intrusion Detection and Investigation using Whole-system Provenance" (S&P 2024) aimed at practical, whole-system detection and investigation together. Taken as a whole, the area moved from foundational shocks to isolation guarantees (Meltdown, ERIM, TrustZone), through systematic kernel bug discovery (MoonShine, Razzer, HFL, Krace), and converged on increasingly automated, machine-learning-driven analysis of system audit data as the dominant frontier for detecting stealthy, long-running intrusions.

milestones.title: Meltdown: Reading Kernel Memory from User Space
milestones.note: shattered hardware memory isolation between user and kernel space, launching the microarchitectural-security era

milestones.title: Debloating Software through Piece-Wise Compilation and Loading
milestones.note: established attack-surface reduction by stripping unused code from binaries and libraries

milestones.title: HOLMES: Real-Time APT Detection through Correlation of Suspicious Information Flows
milestones.note: made provenance-based APT detection real-time, anchoring the dominant audit-graph research thread

milestones.title: ERIM: Secure, Efficient In-process Isolation with Protection Keys (MPK)
milestones.note: demonstrated low-overhead intra-process isolation using hardware memory protection keys

milestones.title: Razzer: Finding Kernel Race Bugs through Fuzzing
milestones.note: extended kernel fuzzing to the hard class of concurrency and data-race bugs

milestones.title: Unicorn: Runtime Provenance-Based Detector for Advanced Persistent Threats
milestones.note: advanced runtime, learning-driven provenance analysis for low-and-slow APTs

milestones.title: SoK: Understanding the Prevailing Security Vulnerabilities in TrustZone-assisted TEE Systems
milestones.note: systematized the fragility of widely deployed TrustZone TEEs, tempering enclave optimism

milestones.title: Kairos: Practical Intrusion Detection and Investigation using Whole-system Provenance
milestones.note: represents the current frontier unifying practical detection and investigation over whole-system provenance
